subject: Aligning promo credits with milestone-based invoicing
messages:
From: Samira Khan <samira@orbitallabs.ai>

Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Promo credits & milestone billing question

Hi Evelyn —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Quick operational question as we pull the contract together for the Orbital Labs accelerator: our program invoices are milestone-based (3 invoices over 6 months). Orbital received the $15k promotional credit you offered during sign-up — we were hoping to apply that credit against the milestone invoices rather than as a one-time prepay/consumption credit.

Can you confirm:
- whether Redwood can allocate promo credits across milestone invoices (e.g., apply $5k to each of the three milestone invoices)
- whether credits are applied at invoice generation or as post-invoice credit notes
- any accounting/tax implications we should expect if credits are delivered as discounts vs credit notes

I attached the draft accelerator agreement so you can see the milestone schedule. If possible, please propose one recommended approach and a fallback we can live with.

Attachments: accelerator_agreement_draft.pdf

Best,
Samira Khan

samira@orbitallabs.ai

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Promo credits & milestone billing question

Hi Samira —

Really good question and thanks for attaching the agreement — that makes the milestone cadence clear. Short answer: yes, we can make promo credits behave the way you described, but there are two pragmatic paths depending on accounting preferences:

Option A — Escrowed allocation (recommended)
- We earmark the $15k promo credit in our billing system and allocate it across the three milestone invoices (e.g., $5k per invoice).
- At invoice generation time the credit reduces the invoice balance; finance issues a normal invoice with line items and a credit allocation.
- Benefits: clean presentation on each invoice, predictable revenue recognition for you and for us.
- Requirements: a short amendment that lists milestone dates and allocation percentages.

Option B — Post-invoice credit note (fallback)
- We generate full invoices per the milestone schedule, then issue credit notes equal to the allocated amounts after each invoice.
- Benefits: minimal change to our invoice generation flow.
- Downsides: slightly more back-and-forth and your AP team might prefer the credit be on the invoice itself.

Accounting/tax note: both approaches are standard. Structurally a credit applied at invoice time reads as a bilateral discount; a post-invoice credit note is an accounts receivable adjustment. If Orbital needs a grant-style treatment (not a discount), we can add language in the amendment to clarify purpose/terms. Finance prefers Option A for clarity, but we can do B if you prefer.

Two quick operational asks from my side:
- Can you confirm the milestone dates you want used for allocation? (I pulled the dates in the draft but want confirmation before we create an amendment)
- Are you asking for any change to Redwood’s promo credit expiry window? Our standard is 90 days after issuance unless specified in a program addendum.

I attached a simple sample billing schedule that shows how Option A would look. If you like it, I’ll loop in Contracts and send a brief two-sentence amendment for signature.

Attachments: sample-billing-schedule.xlsx

Cheers,
Evelyn Hart
Director, Startup Partnerships | Redwood Inference
evelyn@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-6210
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 4 Mar 2027 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Promo credits & milestone billing question

E — quick internal note on accounting/legal tradeoffs (copying Laura so she sees the ask):

- Finance preference: Option A (escrowed allocation) — reduces manual credit notes and keeps monthly AR tidy.
- Legal/tax: they want a clause that caps total applied credits to the promotional amount, and an explicit expiry/forfeiture term if milestones slip >120 days without mutual consent. That protects revenue recognition windows.
- Alternative to avoid credit accounting: offer an upfront one-time discount on milestone 1 (e.g., reduce invoice 1 by $15k) and call the rest of the milestones full price. This is sometimes cleaner from a tax audit perspective but less aligned to the customer ask to spread the benefit.

My proposed next steps:
1) If Samira confirms Option A and milestone dates, Contracts drafts a 1-paragraph amendment allocating $5k per milestone (or %s) and sets expiry to 12 months from issuance (if Samira requests extended window).
2) Laura to check any billing system constraints if expiry != 90 days.
3) We confirm with Orbital whether they want the credits on-invoice vs credit notes — that determines process.

Thoughts?
-Ben
